deities: Chamunda Devi (fierce form of Goddess Durga/Kali)
Lord Shiva as Nandikeshwar (lingam in the cave-like shrine behind the main temple)
Lord Bhairav and Lord Hanuman (guardians flanking the main shrine)
festivals: Navratri (Chaitra and Shardiya - the temple draws large crowds)

history.dynasty: Katoch (Kangra royal house); present structure associated with Raja Umed Singh of Chamba (1762) per some sources
history.period: Present riverside temple dated 1762 CE by some sources; idol relocation legend places the move ~400 years ago; older Aadi Himani Chamunda shrine on the hilltop is much older
history.summary: Chamunda Devi Temple (Chamunda Nandikeshwar Dham) stands on the banks of the Baner river in Dharamshala Tehsil, dedicated to the goddess Chamunda, the fierce form of Durga who slew the demons Chanda and Munda (hence the name). The much older original shrine, Aadi Himani Chamunda, sits on a hilltop ~16 km uphill (a 13-km trek); the deity was moved to the present accessible site when a 16th-century king and priest received the goddess's consent in a dream and recovered a buried idol - a legend, though some sources date the present temple to 1762 under Raja Umed Singh of Chamba, while others claim a 700-year antiquity (conflict - verify). The main idol is kept concealed under a red cloth. Wikipedia notes it is not among the classical 51 Shakti Peethas, though it is counted among Himachal's five major Shakti temples. Derelict and fire-damaged until 1991, it was restored from 1992 by devotee P. D. Saini over ~20 years. FLAG: CSV town 'Dharamshala' is imprecise; the temple is at Chamunda village (Padar), ~14-15 km from Dharamshala on the Dharamshala-Palampur road.

name: Chamunda Devi Temple
town_description: Chamunda is a small town in Dharamshala Tehsil of Kangra district on the Dharamshala-Palampur road, set on the banks of the Baner river with the Dhauladhar peaks as backdrop.

travel.airport: Kangra Airport (Gaggal, DHM), about 30 km from the temple (verify).
travel.railway: Chamunda Marg station on the narrow-gauge Kangra Valley Railway is nearby; nearest major railhead is Pathankot Junction, about 85 km.
travel.road: On the Dharamshala-Palampur road: about 14-15 km from Dharamshala, 19 km from Palampur, 24 km from McLeod Ganj; combine with Kangra Fort (10 km away).

visitor_information.best_time: March to June for pleasant weather; Navratri (March-April and September-October) brings grand celebrations and large crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Summer 5:00 AM-12:00 PM and 1:00-10:00 PM; winter 6:00 AM-12:00 PM and 1:00-9:00 PM; closed 12:00-1:00 PM daily for bhog (gokshetra) - verify before visiting. Morning aarti 8:00-8:45 AM, evening aarti 7:10-7:50 PM. Free entry; free langar 12:00-2:00 PM and 7:00-9:00 PM.
